etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English grocerye, equivalent to grocer +‎ -y. Compare gross. Doublet of groceria.

definitions.definition: (attributive) Retail foodstuffs and other household supplies.

quote.citation: 1776: Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations
quote.text: Where ten thousand pounds can be employed in the grocery trade, the wages of the grocer's labour make but a very trifling addition...

definitions.definition: A shop or store that sells groceries; a grocery store.

quote.text: I observed that the vitals of the village were the grocery, the bar-room, the post-office, and the bank...

quote.citation: 1913, George Lee Burton, Tackling Matrimony: To the Men and Girls who Love Each Other More than Ease and Show and Sham‎[1]:
quote.text: We shopped and groceried on a cash basis, determined on that from the start.

quote.citation: 1967, The New Yorker‎[2], volume 43, number 5, page 210:
quote.text: The thought of grocerying so casually at Seessel's evokes a giggle from Shirley

quote.citation: 2012, Hazel Rae Minnick, Living in My Shadow‎[3], page 93:
quote.text: I was dependent upon others for grocerying and getting to doctor appointments.

quote.citation: [2016 July 19, “The word of the week: grocerying”, in StarTribune.com‎[4]:
quote.text: Sample usage: "If you're going grocerying, pick up some GMO — you know, Goat's Milk, Organic. But it has to be non-GMO GMO."]

quote.citation: 1939, John Willy, Hotel Monthly‎[5], volume 47, number 550, page 59:
quote.text: Fifty-eight years of grocerying hotels, restaurants and institutions that feed many people

quote.citation: 1998, Ron Rau, “Doing It for Money”, in David Seybold, editor, Seasons of the Angler: A Fisherman's Anthology, page 95:
quote.text: What freedom to be iced, fueled, and groceried for two weeks and running toward a reef you truly love
